title: AI-Trader: Benchmarking Autonomous Agents in Real-Time Financial Markets

task.value: A live, fully autonomous, data-uncontaminated benchmark for evaluating LLM agents' financial trading decisions across U.S. stocks, A-shares and cryptocurrencies.
task.quote: we introduce AI-Trader, the first fully-automated, live, and data-uncontaminated evaluation benchmark for LLM agents in financial decision-making.

architecture.value: Decoupled live trading environment and ReAct-style trading agents with minimal context (prices, holdings, tools), using MCP tools: Check Price, Search, News, Math, Trade; Buy/Sell/Hold actions with rejection and self-correction on liquidity violations.
architecture.quote: The AI-Trader framework consists of two fully decoupled components: the Live Trading Environment (Sec.3.1) and the Trading Agents (Sec. 3.2).

data.value: Nasdaq-100 constituents plus cash (hourly), SSE-50 constituents (daily), and 10 USDT crypto pairs tracked by the Bitwise Index (daily); prices, web search and financial news via tools.
data.quote: We employ a daily-frequency strategy for trading A-shares and cryptocurrencies, while monitoring and recording U.S. equity trades using an hourly-frequency strategy.

window.value: Live trading: U.S. equities and A-shares October 1, 2025 to November 7, 2025; cryptocurrency November 1 to November 14, 2025. No training split (benchmark of pretrained LLMs).
window.quote: we present live trading results for U.S. equities and A-shares from October 1, 2025, to November 7, 2025, along with a detailed evaluation and analysis of the cryptocurrency market from November 1 to November 14, 2025.

models.value: DeepSeek-v3.1, MiniMax-M2, Claude-3.7-sonnet, GPT-5, Qwen3-max, Gemini-2.5-flash, each wrapped in identical agents.
models.quote: The AI-Trader employs six mainstream models as baselines: DeepSeek-v3.1 (Liu et al., 2024), MiniMax-M2 (MiniMax, 2025), Claude-3.7-sonnet (Anthropic, 2025a) , GPT-5 (OpenAI, 2025), Qwen3-max (Yang et al., 2025), and Gemini-2.5-flash (Comanici et al., 2025).

baselines.value: Market benchmarks: QQQ Invesco (U.S.), SSE-50 index (A-shares), CD5 Index (crypto); LLMs compared against each other.
baselines.quote: AI trading strategies more easily generate excess returns in highly liquid markets. In the U.S. market, multiple AI agents achieved positive excess returns: MiniMax-M2 (+7.69% excess), DeepSeek-v3.1 (+6.52% excess), and even Claude-3.7-Sonnet (+1.24% excess) all outperformed QQQ.

headline_result.value: U.S. market (Oct 1–Nov 7, 2025, hourly): MiniMax-M2 cumulative return 9.56% vs QQQ 1.87%, Sortino 4.42, MDD -4.92%; no agent beat SSE-50 (1.65%); in crypto only DeepSeek-v3.1 beat CD5 (-12.18% vs -14.30%).
headline_result.quote: In the U.S. market, MiniMax-M2 achieves a cumulative return of 9.56% (significantly higher than QQQ’s 1.87%) and the highest Sortino ratio among all models at 4.42, while limiting maximum drawdown to -4.92%, outperforming all AI models except the benchmark.

leakage_controls.value: Live evaluation in real time; Search tool strictly limited to information available up to the current simulated time to prevent future data leakage.
leakage_controls.quote: strictly limited to information available up to the current simulated time—to prevent data leakage from the future and support AI in fundamental or event-driven analysis.

limitations.value: Agents lack a systematic information verification module and can be swayed by single news sources; poor returns, weak risk management and poor cross-market generalization of current agents.
limitations.quote: the decision-making mechanism lacks a systematic information verification module, making it prone to forming judgments based on a single information source, which can easily lead to misjudgments in highly volatile and information-dense market conditions.

release.value: Code and evaluation data open-sourced on GitHub.
release.quote: The code and evaluation data are open-sourced to foster community research: https://github.com/HKUDS/AI-Trader.
